ideas: Protecting people from fake images and misinformation
Whether labelling laws could realistically be enforced
How attitudes to AI content might change

phrases.meaning: see how two things are different
an obvious sign showing what something is

model: I'd say yes, it should be labelled by law, at least for images, videos and news content. The main reason is that AI is getting so good that most people simply can't tell the difference anymore. A deepfake of a politician could easily mislead the public just before an election, and without a clear label, it's going to erode trust in everything we see online. I remember seeing a photo last year of a famous building on fire, and I shared it with my family before realising it was completely generated by AI. I felt quite embarrassed. If companies were required to label it, they'd be held accountable when things go wrong. Of course, critics argue that it's hard to enforce, because content moves across borders and people can remove labels quite easily. That's a fair point. But I think we need to strike a balance, and a law is still a good starting point. In ten years, I suspect labels will be completely normal, just like nutrition information on food.
